list.name: Vivi Music 6.0.8.9_DE 1.54.32
list.body:
## Vivi Music 6.0.8.9_DE 1.54.32
**Release channel:** `beta`

### 🔧 Changed
- [DE] **Theme & Colors is one screen built around the wheel: the picker's controls are beside it, the palette is six per row, and the accent intensity lives there alone (issue #103).** The section held the same setting twice and stood two screens tall: the intensity was a full-width slider in a block of its own, under it a row of five preview circles showing the value the slider already showed, and the custom-colour picker sat further down with a *Hide* label of its own. The layout the owner drew and approved is what it is now: the palette and the saved custom colours on the left (rows of six, with the custom-colour circle as the last swatch of the flow), the wheel on the right with its brightness strip and, rightmost, the accent intensity as a vertical strip - the one control that sets it - captioned and showing its percentage; the live HEX field and *Add to palette* under the wheel, centred with it; the intensity slider, its five preview circles and the second *Custom color* block are gone, and the picker opens with the screen. The palette column keeps a fixed width (`PickerColumnWidth`: the wheel, the two strips and the widest caption) because a full-width row inside an **unweighted** column takes the whole Row and left the wheel rendering at `x = 0`, which the render check reported. **Measured:** `:desktop:compileKotlin`, `:desktop:compileTestKotlin` pass; `:desktop:colorWheelRenderCheck`, extended to the new layout so it reads the pixels instead of an offset that was guessed: `wheel blob: 220x220px, 37155px of ink, at 640,412`, `rim: right=(255,52,53) bottom=(152,255,52) left=(50,254,255) top=(151,50,255)`, `marker: green=(695, 614) red=(856, 521)`, `strip: top=(0,236,0) middle=(0,128,0)`, `strips right of the wheel: 20x180px at 874, 20x146px at 944`, `intensity: top=(12,243,12) bottom=(124,132,124)`, `palette: 24 round swatch(es) left of the wheel`, `under the wheel: 1 round swatch(es)` - `OK`. **Watch:** the wheel must sit right of the palette, with the brightness strip, then the intensity strip, then the hex field and the button under the wheel; dragging one of the three controls must move only its own value, and *Hide* must put the whole picker aside leaving the palette in place. **Open sub-item:** the check measures position and ink, not the live theme; the colour the strips produce is still the one `adjustAccentIntensity` applies.

### 🐛 Fixed
- [DE] **The account's liked list is no longer fetched and thrown away on every sync, and *Sync playlist* adopts the account's playlist instead of creating a second one (issue #102).** Two failures with one root each, both visible in the owner's own files. **The discarded lists:** the pull printed `10 playlist(s) in the account (2 new, 8 already here and checked for songs added on YouTube Music)` and the two "new" ones never became anything, because `PlaylistStore.applyRemote` refuses the account's own special lists - `LM`, *Liked Music*, and `SE`, *Episodes for Later* (the phone has its own Liked list and its own saved-for-later row, and mirroring the desktop's copy over gave it a second entry for each) - so the pull mirrored both playlists with their songs and then dropped them, on **every run the log holds: 46 in one week, 21 to 25 per list, `'Liked Music': 11 song(s) mirrored (new)` and `'Episodes for Later': 0 song(s) mirrored (new)`**. They are filtered out before the fetch now, the count of them is logged (`2 special list(s) not mirrored on purpose`) and the test that decides this lives in one place (`SPECIAL_ACCOUNT_PLAYLISTS`, now `internal`). The same line was also wrong about the lists that *are* here: "already here" was matched on `SyncedPlaylist.remoteId` alone, while a playlist mirrored from the account carries its account id inside its own id (`yt-<id>`), so every mirror read as new on every run and was re-downloaded and re-compared for nothing. Both stored forms count now (`accountPlaylistId()`), the same the device sync compares with. **The duplicate:** `PlaylistSync.accountPlaylistNamed` returned only an account playlist that no local row had claimed, so for a name the account already held (the owner's `nigga`, six rows over four distinct account ids in `~/.vivimusic/playlists.json`) the lookup came back empty and `pushOne` created the playlist on YouTube Music a second time. A claimed copy is now the fallback answer, so the existing playlist is adopted, and the local rows collapse into one entry - with `repairDuplicates(prefer)` keeping the row that was just linked, which is the playlist the create dialog has navigated to, instead of tombstoning it under the user. **Measured:** `:desktop:compileKotlin`, `:desktop:compileTestKotlin` pass. **Watch:** run *Sync playlist* on a name YouTube Music already has: no second playlist may appear on the account, and the two local rows must become one; `playlists.log` must show the special lists in the count instead of a pair that is fetched and dropped. **Open sub-item:** the two local rows merge into one, so a same-named local playlist whose songs differ is merged (union) rather than kept apart, as `samePlaylist` documents.

### 📝 Commits
- v6.0.8.9_DE-1.54.32: Theme & Colors rebuilt, playlist duplicates fixed

---
This release was built automatically from commit `ce6a0c726ddf9d46a22aab619c423ffb93d45bea`.

list.body:
## Vivi Music 6.0.8.9_DE 1.54.31
**Release channel:** `beta`

### 🔧 Changed
- [APK] **French and Azerbaijani are complete: every key the app declares now reads in those two languages.** "traduci interamente il apk in tutte le lingue in cui esso è disponibile": an audit of the whole resource tree (56 locale folders against the four base files) finds **50,916 missing (locale, key) pairs**, and the two smallest are closed here: French was missing 23 strings and Azerbaijani 103, almost all of them the app's own recent work that had been added to English only (the device sync screen and its two volume channels, the listening summary, the player design and crossfade settings, SponsorBlock, the custom font, the settings subtitles). A reusable filler now applies a translation pack to the locale files (`app/src/main/res/values-*/`), refusing a key no base string declares and refusing any translation whose `%`-placeholders do not match the English one, and it escapes the apostrophes aapt2 requires, so a batch of translations cannot reintroduce the build failure fixed in 6.0.8.8. **Measured:** the filler added 95 strings with 0 refused (31 of the 126 keys were already translated in another file of the same locale folder, and adding them again fails the resource merger with `Duplicate resources`), the escape scanner reports 0 problems over every `values*/` file, `:app:mergeUniversalFossReleaseResources` passes and `:app:compileUniversalFossReleaseKotlin` passes. **Watch:** French and Azerbaijani must show every screen in their own language with no English left; the audit must report `0` missing for `values-fr` and `values-az`. **Open sub-item:** the remaining 50,916 pairs are tracked in `TODO.md`, most of them one language at a time (the smallest next: Brazilian Portuguese 109, Swedish 110, Turkish 371, Japanese 524).

### 📝 Commits
- v6.0.8.9_DE-1.54.31: French and Azerbaijani complete, translation filler

list.name: Vivi Music 6.0.8.8_DE 1.54.31
list.body:
## Vivi Music 6.0.8.8_DE 1.54.31
**Release channel:** `beta`

### 🐛 Fixed
- [APK] **The release APK builds again: the string that failed aapt2 is escaped.** "non capisco perché il workflow dell'apk sia fallito, sistemalo" - the failed run (`Build Android APK`, 15:31) ends in `Execution failed for task ':app:mergeUniversalFossReleaseResources'` and, in the diagnostic lines above it, `app/src/main/res/values-en-rCA/strings.xml: Failed to flatten XML for resource 'sync_native_volume_desc' with error: Invalid unicode escape sequence in string`, with the same line for `values-pa`. The cause is in the text itself: `sync_native_volume_desc` carried **unescaped apostrophes** (`the operating system's own volume`, `each device's`, and the Punjabi `ਬੰਦ ਕਰਨ 'ਤੇ`), which aapt2 refuses - the neighbouring `sync_vivi_volume_desc` had escaped them (`device\'s`) and this one did not, so the resource never compiled. The string was rewritten in all six locales that have it (`values`, `en-rCA`, `pa`, `bn-rIN`, `fi`, `ml`), and two more aapt2 hazards found by scanning every `values*/` file for the same defects were fixed with it: a `\v` escape where a paragraph break was meant (`discord_information` in `values`, `az`, `sv`, the French `\V`) and a `\’` escape before a typographic apostrophe (French `jiosaavn_beta_info`). **Measured:** `:app:mergeUniversalFossReleaseResources` on the previous text reproduces the CI error (`Failed to flatten XML for resource 'sync_native_volume_desc'`, `BUILD FAILED`) and passes on the new one (`BUILD SUCCESSFUL`); `:app:compileUniversalFossReleaseKotlin` passes. **Watch:** the next `Build Android APK` run must reach the APK upload on both flavors. **Open sub-item:** no phone here, so the strings are checked as resources, not as they read on a device.
- [APK] **A playlist's own songs are re-read from the account, so a song added on YouTube Music from another device shows up, and a row named after its own videoId is repaired.** "le playlist continuano a non aggiornarsi ... la playlist 'nigga' l'ho creata da pc attivando la sync con youtube music, poi ci ho aggiunto brani su mobile ma nonostante ciò questi brani che ho aggiunto su mobile non vengono visualizzati su apk". `executeSyncSavedPlaylists` read an existing playlist's row for its name and its thumbnail and then stopped: the full re-read behind it was gated by `playlistEntity.isAutoSync`, a column that **no code path in the app ever sets to true** (only the default `false` and three reads exist), so the branch that fetched a playlist's songs was unreachable and a song added to the account elsewhere could never arrive. It now always re-reads the playlist's songs (`executeRefreshPlaylist`), with the same merge the desktop applies (`refreshLinked`): the songs the account holds and this copy does not are **appended**, the local order is kept, and a local-only song is deliberately never removed (the app does not push removals to the account, so adopting the account's shorter list would undo the user's own edit here). The same response also repairs a row whose stored title is blank or is its own id - the "code" that first arrived through the liked-songs device sync (`title = entry.title.ifBlank { id }`) and that a playlist then displayed as the song's name - so the repair no longer depends on that song being liked. **Measured:** `:app:compileUniversalFossReleaseKotlin` passes. **Watch:** add a song to a playlist on YouTube Music from the phone, then open Playlists in the app: the song must appear (the log line is `refreshPlaylist: Added N song(s) the account had and the phone did not (<browseId>)`) without the playlist losing its order, and no row may read like a videoId (`refreshPlaylist: Repaired the name of <id>`). **Open sub-item:** a removal made on YouTube Music still does not remove the song on the phone, deliberately, as on the desktop.

### 📝 Commits
- v6.0.8.8_DE-1.54.31: build the APK again, re-read playlists

---
This release was built automatically from commit `e0b2a4e561f93b158e52893c0bbf421e152c0f05`.

list.name: Vivi Music 6.0.8.7_DE 1.54.31
list.body:
## Vivi Music 6.0.8.7_DE 1.54.31
**Release channel:** `beta`

### 🐛 Fixed
- [DE] **The account's playlists are re-read while the app is open, so a song added on YouTube Music from the phone arrives without a restart.** "[DE] la cosa delle playlist di youtube music di prima persiste perché io ho aggiunto canzoni da mobile a una playlist youtube music e questa continua e non venire aggiornata su DE": the previous release made the pull read the playlists it already has (`refreshLinked`, so a song added there is added here), but the pull itself only ever ran **once at startup** (and behind the settings switch). The reporter's own `playlists.log` shows the shape of it: the startup run at 16:40:15 pulled `'4': 1 song(s) added on YouTube Music were pulled into the local playlist`, and every song he added after that - with the app still open - had nothing that would ever ask the account again. A timer now re-reads the account every five minutes while signed in with *Auto sync with account* on, and each run is logged with the same `youtube sync (periodic): N playlist(s) in the account (…, … checked for songs added on YouTube Music)` line the manual run writes, so the next report can be read from `playlists.log` alone. A run that finds nothing still writes nothing, which keeps the `updatedAt` of an untouched playlist intact for the device sync's last-write-wins. **Watch:** add a song to any of your playlists on YouTube Music from the phone and leave the desktop open: within five minutes `playlists.log` must show the periodic run and `'<name>': N song(s) added on YouTube Music were pulled into the local playlist`, and the playlist must show the new song without losing its own order. **Open sub-item:** a removal made on YouTube Music still does not remove the song here, as before.
- [DE] **A playlist the phone edited without a timestamp is no longer half-merged.** The device sync merges a playlist by last-write-wins on `updatedAt`, and a phone build older than 1.54.29 never moved that timestamp when a song was added - so the two sides carry the **same** edit time with **different** songs, and on that tie the desktop kept its own copy and dropped the phone's songs. The owner's own store shows exactly that state: `nigga` has 5 songs on the phone and 2 on the desktop, both with `updatedAt = 1791823661501`. An equal edit time with a different song list is now merged instead of decided: the local order stays, the songs only the peer holds are appended, and a song both sides have stays once (a playlist that is simply re-pushed, which is the common case, changes nothing at all). Nothing is removed by it - a removal carries no "which side is newer" on a tie - so the worst case is a song the phone deleted staying here, never a song of yours disappearing. **Watch:** after installing this build, `nigga` (and any other playlist in that state) must show the union of the two: the phone's extra songs appear here, in their own order at the end, and nothing is lost from either side. **Open sub-item:** the healing is per-pairing and local to the desktop; a new edit made with the updated APK travels by its own timestamp and does not need it.
- [DE] **Issue #3 while NOT paired: the ~200 ms the audio writer was losing every 30 seconds is gone.** The owner's own finding is that the stutter also happens with no device paired, and his 1.54.29 session (`~/.vivimusic/logs/20261013-163826/`) contains it in a single line: `audio priority stall: 50ms sleep returned 221ms late (= 171ms held up at the writer's priority; heap 118/2048MB, gc … worst 214ms, total 878ms in 37 pauses; cpu 13% of 59% busy …)`. The writer was not starved by load (13 % of 59 % busy) and the heap was 118 MB of 2 GB, and the `gc.log` of the same session shows what did it: a `System.gc()` **every 30.0 s** (`16:49:58.990`, `16:50:29.297`, `16:50:59.408`, …) - that is Skiko's own memory trim - each one followed by a `G1 Concurrent GC` event of 33 / 104 / 120 / **214 ms**, and the 214 ms one is the stall above. `-XX:+ExplicitGCInvokesConcurrent` (the earlier answer) only made the pause concurrent in name: the cycle still stops the world for its remark phase. The call is now ignored outright (`-XX:+DisableExplicitGC`), so the every-30-s event disappears instead of being reshaped, and G1 keeps collecting on its own heuristics. `GcMonitor` reports it honestly too: a `G1 Concurrent GC` notification describes a whole cycle, not a pause, and it is no longer logged as "every thread was stopped here" (the writer's own measurement is what says a stall happened). **Watch:** with nothing paired, play a track for a few minutes: `gc.log` must show no `System.gc()`-caused event every 30 s, `playback.log` must not carry a `gc cycle`/`gc pause` line larger than a young pause, and no `audio priority stall` line must appear while `audio device check` keeps reading ~100 %. **Open sub-item:** the flag removes the periodic disturbance; a long stop-the-world pause from G1's own young collections (5-70 ms in that session) remains possible and is what the 8 s PCM queue absorbs.
- [APK] **The Device sync screen is a Material 3 Expressive screen, and both volume channels are on it.** "rifai la schermata del device sync di mobile, rifalla con cards eccetera, full material3 e material3 expressive, con opzioni di volume (sia vivi sia os)": the screen was a column of loose rows - a title, one switch, a text field, four buttons and two labels - with no card structure at all, and the second volume channel was not reachable from anywhere in the UI. It is now three Material 3 blocks: a **state card** that answers "is this phone connected, and to what" in one glance (the paired/not-paired title, a `Badge` when paired, the peer device's name, the live relay status line, and Unpair inside the card), a **connection card** (relay address, *Find desktop* and *Scan QR code* as filled tonal buttons with the discovery spinner in place, and the six-digit code with *Pair* - drawn only while not paired, so the card never offers Pair and Unpair at once), and the project's own `ExpressiveSettingGroup` for the **volume section**: *Sync VIVI volume* (the in-app slider) and *Sync OS volume* (the operating system's own media volume), each its own data-store key, with two new fully translated strings. **Measured:** `:app:compileUniversalFossDebugKotlin` passes. **Watch:** open Settings → Device sync unpaired and paired: the state card must change colour and content, the code row must disappear once paired, and both switches must persist across a restart (they are `SyncViviVolumeKey` / `SyncNativeVolumeKey`, the keys `MusicService` reads when it publishes the volume to the peer). **Open sub-item:** no phone here, so the layout is compile-verified only.

### 📝 Commits
- v6.0.8.7_DE-1.54.31: the account's playlists are re-read while the app is open, a playlist the phone edited without a timestamp is merged, issue #3 unpaired is fixed, and the device sync screen is Material 3 Expressive with both volume channels
- v6.0.8.6_DE-1.54.30: no more a videoId where a song's name belongs on the phone, and the rows already stored that way are repaired
- v6.0.8.6_DE-1.54.29: the YouTube Music sync reads the playlists it already has, a playlist edited on the phone reaches the DE, and the audio is no longer restarted every 5 seconds

---
This release was built automatically from commit `cb6375477eb4a36064a7f212f16c8a2b16611004`.

list.name: Vivi Music 6.0.8.6_DE 1.54.30
list.body:
## Vivi Music 6.0.8.6_DE 1.54.30
**Release channel:** `beta`

### 🐛 Fixed
- [APK] **The "code" the phone showed instead of a song's name is gone, and the rows that already carry it are repaired.** Asked what the name looked like, the owner answered with the whole mechanism in one sentence: *"sembra l'url del brano, in teoria e' lo stesso nome del file che viviDE salva su windows"*. That string is a **videoId** - the desktop's own audio cache on Windows is called `<videoId>.m4a` - and there was exactly one place in the app that wrote one where a title belongs: `applyRemoteLikedSongs` stored an arriving like it knew nothing about as `title = entry.title.ifBlank { id }`. The desktop sends its liked library to the phone as a flat list of ids by design (`LibrarySnapshot.songIds`, the field an older peer reads), so *every* like in that list landed here named after its own id - and nothing could ever correct it, because the phone's own account sync (the only path that fetches a liked song's real metadata) did not refresh an existing row's title at all. Two changes: a like that arrives with no metadata is no longer named after its videoId (the like is still stored - that is what travelled - and the title is left empty on purpose instead of being filled with a wrong name), and the account sync now refreshes the metadata of a liked row whose title is blank **or equal to its own id**, so the rows already stored that way are repaired by the next liked-songs sync and the empty ones are filled. **Measured:** `:app:compileUniversalFossDebugKotlin` passes. **Watch:** after a liked-songs sync on the phone, no row in the liked list may read like a videoId, and a song whose row was stored that way must show its real title. **Open sub-item:** the repair reaches the rows the phone's own account sync covers (an account like) - a like that exists only in the device sync's ledger keeps the empty title, which is still better than a wrong name, and the log names it (`liked song '<id>' arrived with no metadata`).

### 📝 Commits
- v6.0.8.6_DE-1.54.30: il "codice" al posto del nome di un brano sul telefono non c'è più, e le righe già scritte così vengono riparate

---
